derivation: Independent derivation with Python's standard-library zoneinfo (expected/derive_time.py; IANA data, no Spark). New York is UTC-05:00 until 2026-03-08 07:00:00Z, when clocks move from 02:00 EST to 03:00 EDT (UTC-04:00), and returns to UTC-05:00 at 2026-11-01 06:00:00Z, when 02:00 EDT becomes 01:00 EST so that 01:00-01:59 occurs twice. Events: e1 04:30Z -> 03-07 23:30 -05:00 (local day 03-07, local hour 23, UTC day 03-08); e2 05:00Z -> 03-08 00:00 -05:00 (hour 0); e3 05:30Z -> 00:30 -05:00 (0); e4 06:45Z -> 01:45 -05:00 (1); e5 06:00Z -> 01:00 -05:00 (1); e6 08:00Z -> 04:00 -04:00 (4); e7 2026-04-01 03:30Z -> 03-31 23:30 -04:00 (local March, hour 23, UTC April); e8 04:10Z -> 04-01 00:10 -04:00 (0). Under a UTC session every event renders as its stored instant with offset Z and its UTC hour. Downtime pairs (STOP followed by START per machine): M1 23:30->00:00 = 30 elapsed and 30 wall-clock minutes, attributed to local day 03-07; M1 00:30->01:45 = 75/75 on 03-08; M2 01:00 EST -> 04:00 EDT = 120 elapsed minutes (06:00Z to 08:00Z) but 180 wall-clock minutes because the clock skipped 02:00-03:00; M3 23:30->00:10 = 40/40 on 03-31. Subtracting the two M2 timestamps gives the local-clock difference, 3 hours, printed in Spark's day-time interval format INTERVAL '0 03:00:00' DAY TO SECOND (the format and the local-clock rule were recorded from this build); under UTC the same subtraction is 2 hours. DST day facts: local 03-07 spans 24 wall-clock and 24 elapsed hours; 03-08 spans 24 wall-clock hours but 23 elapsed hours; 03-09 24/24. 2026-03-07 12:00 EST plus one calendar day is 03-08 12:00 EDT (23 hours later); plus 24 elapsed hours is 03-08 13:00 EDT. The local string 2026-03-08 02:30:00 does not exist: this build moves it forward to 03:30 -04:00, the gap rule the Databricks archive page on Spark 3 dates describes (recorded as observed); the same string cast to TIMESTAMP_NTZ keeps 02:30:00 because no zone is applied. Fall-back night: a synthetic stoppage from 05:30Z (01:30 EDT) to 06:15Z (01:15 EST) lasts 45 elapsed minutes while the local clock reads 15 minutes backwards (-15); the ambiguous local string 2026-11-01 01:30:00 resolves to the earlier offset, -04:00, as the same archive page describes (recorded as observed). Month attribution: M3's 40 minutes fall in local month 2026-03 but UTC month 2026-04.
